subject: 🏃 Thursday — 10 mi Progression Run (Wk 10 Peak)
html:
Tomorrow you have a 10-mile progression run — 8 miles easy, then 2 miles at threshold. This is the biggest midweek run of the entire build. 17 days to race day.

HR governs. Easy block (mi 1–8): ≤145 BPM (Z2), pace readout ~9:00 on the hilly door route — let it float freely. Threshold finish (mi 9–10): HR 155–165 BPM, cap 165, pace readout ~7:15–7:25 — accept whatever the hills give you at correct HR.

Pre-run activation + posterior-chain warm-up: Hip CARs, banded lateral walks, glute bridges, banded hip IR (5–10/side), then the hamstring protocol: 2×10 dynamic leg swings per side (forward/back + lateral), 10 walking hamstring reaches per side, 10 glute bridges. Foam-roll posterior chain before heading out.

Hamstring gate (non-negotiable): If the right hamstring twinges during the easy block, skip the progression finish — run the last 2 miles easy instead. Three faint appearances in 11 days means we respect it, not test it. Protecting the hamstring for Sunday's 20-miler is the priority; the threshold dose is expendable.

Hydration: Carry a handheld (~14–16 oz water + a pinch of LMNT, ~250 mg sodium). Sip every 15–20 min. Ten hilly miles will run ~85 min — don't repeat the underfueled pattern from July 5. Eat a proper dinner tonight and a normal pre-run breakfast 2–3 hours out.

Focus cue: Save the legs on the descents — quick cadence, short stride, no bombing downhill. The hilly door route is SF rehearsal, and controlled descents protect both the knee and the hamstring.

Where you are: Week 10 of 12, Phase 3 Peak Volume — the biggest week of the build (~48 mi). Tuesday's track and today's easy recovery set the table; this is the second quality session. Sunday's 20-miler is the race-format referendum — the run that decides Full vs. First Half. Get through tomorrow clean and you're perfectly positioned for that dress rehearsal. Bed by 10, set the alarm, lay out your gear tonight.
